## Generated API clients

When OpenAPI client generation is adopted: treat generated code as generated, keep it separate from handwritten feature logic, regenerate it when the contract changes, and do not patch generated files unless the generation workflow requires it (`swagger` skill for contract concerns).

## Testing

Useful targets: meaningful component behavior, validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior, complex reactive state. Do not test framework internals or duplicate the same behavior at every level. E2E tests (Playwright, when adopted) focus on a small number of important user workflows unless broader coverage is required.

- **Migrations:** create schema changes as new EF Core migrations from the Infrastructure project with the Api project as startup project, for example `dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project backend/<Name>.Infrastructure --startup-project backend/<Name>.Api`. Treat migrations as source code: review each generated migration before committing it, paying particular attention to destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys, and delete behavior.
- **Tests:** changed behavior gets maintained automated coverage at the right level (`0-core/testing-principles.md`).

Application Services can be unit-tested with controlled repository and external-service doubles; assert the use-case result and meaningful side effects. "Repository method X was called once" is useful only when that interaction is part of the contract. When behavior depends heavily on EF Core semantics, transactions, DI wiring, serialization, or HTTP, prefer an integration test.

| Scenario | Approach |
|---|---|
| Pure business rule | NUnit unit test |
| Application orchestration | unit test with boundary doubles when useful |
| Full API pipeline | `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` |
| Important EF/provider behavior | integration test on the actual provider |
| Simple API integration, provider irrelevant | lightweight isolated relational database |
| Time-dependent behavior | `TimeProvider` / `FakeTimeProvider` |
| External HTTP dependency | stub handler or local fake server |
| Reproduced bug | focused regression test |
| Deployment/basic health | smoke test |
Swagger as a substitute for integration tests; anonymous objects as long-lived contracts; a second competing documentation stack without a concrete need.
